title: A symmetric Hamburger moment problem with b_(n-1)/b_n<=q<1 eventually has bounded normalized moment/kernel coefficients and the cs-star absolute summability giving an entrywise absolutely convergent reproducing-kernel inverse of its Hankel matrix
author: Christian Berg; Ryszard Szwarc
source_title: Inverse of Infinite Hankel Moment Matrices
difficulty_reason: Infinite Hankel inversion requires absolute control of double sums; finite inverse identities do not justify associating the infinite matrix products. The author proves separate moment and reproducing-kernel coefficient bounds by q-Pochhammer inductions and shows stability under finite initial recurrence changes. Their combination yields superexponential decay of the shifted coefficient-moment products and the strong summability needed for a valid inverse.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: All essential Theorem1.9 support was read: indeterminacy1.7(i), coefficient/matrix setup and Fubini inversion Lemma2.1, moment-coefficient recurrences3.3-3.6 with the eventually q-increasing comparison3.7, inverse coefficient recurrence/shift estimates4.1-4.5, Corollary4.6 and the complete superexponential summability proof5.1. The author separately controls normalized moments U_n and reproducing-kernel diagonal coefficients V_n via two q-Pochhammer induction bounds, handles finite initial perturbations, and obtains c_(2n-j)*s_(2n) decay. This proves the strong cs-star summability condition, which the supplied absolute-double-sum argument turns into the reproducing-kernel inverse identity. All other log-concave thresholds, birth-death counterexample and explicit classical-family variants are uncounted.

statement_scope: Full Theorem1.9 for a symmetric Hamburger probability-moment problem with infinite support and all moments, Jacobi diagonal a_n=0, positive recurrence b_n, and b_(n-1)/b_n<=q for some0<q<1 and all sufficiently large n. Retain definitions U_n=s_(2n)/(b_0^2...b_(n-1)^2), V_n=b_0...b_(n-1)*c_n and c_n=sqrt(A_(n,n)), where A is the reproducing-kernel coefficient matrix. U_n,V_n,c_n*sqrt(s_(2n)) are bounded and sum_l c_l*abs(s_(l+m)) is finite for every m>=0. The supplied Lemma2.1 yields AH=HA=I with entrywise absolute convergence. No bounded-operator inverse interpretation on l2, uniqueness among all infinite inverses or polynomial-growth relaxation is added.
source_boundary_note: The complete original main Theorem 1.9 and all new eventually-q-increasing support are retained as one inverse-Hankel task. The exact moment/coefficient/reproducing-kernel definitions and absolute-double-sum inversion Lemma 2.1 are supplied, together with indeterminacy, both independent q-Pochhammer induction bounds and all finite-initial-perturbation/shift comparisons. The full superexponential shifted coefficient-moment summability establishes cs-star and yields entrywise absolutely convergent AH=HA=I through the supplied author inversion argument. Other log-concave thresholds, cubic counterexamples and explicit-family claims are unselected. No bounded-operator inverse interpretation, uniqueness of infinite inverses or generated argument is asserted.
